cohort: 220 pregnant women, divided into an exposed group with BMI >= 30 kg/m2 (n=110) and a non-exposed control group with BMI < 30 kg/m2 (n=110).
finding: Maternal obesity was significantly associated with increased rates of cesarean section (RR=2.74), PIH (RR=3.08), GDM (RR=1.48), preeclampsia (RR=2), macrosomia (RR=6.85), and shoulder dystocia (RR=4.80), but not low birth weight (p=0.053).
mod_finding: Cesarean section deliveries were 3 times more likely in obese pregnant women (RR=2.74) compared to non-obese pregnant women.
